title: V8 P stage: exp, fused rescale, strided publication
formula: p = hif8(exp(s - m)) for three score tiles, acc = acc * w + pv, published into the packed 33x256 NZ carrier
study_for: The accumulator rescale is one fused instruction, not two: `muldstadd` computes `dst = dst * src0 + src1`, so `acc = acc * old_weight + pv` happens in place. Rows are unrolled so the per-row load -> FMA -> store chains overlap.

Determinism around a strided store. The P stores skip one 32-byte block per fractal column (`block 32 + 33 i`) and the tail writes three rows only, so the kernel zeroes the tiles first. That is what makes every published byte defined, and it is what lets this demo compare whole physical carriers instead of only the live rows — run `--case padding_poison`, which fills the incoming carrier with 0xA5, and watch the answer not move.

Comparing against a SET of admissible answers instead of one. The device's native `exp` is within one measured FP32 ULP of a correctly rounded exp; at a HiFloat8 quantization boundary that one ULP picks the neighbouring code. `reference_candidates` propagates the interval through the same ties-away conversion, and `compare_one_of` prints how many elements actually had two admissible codes. Under sim that number is 0 for every P tile except `padding_poison`'s `p1`, where it is 1 of 8448 — the whole reason the mode exists is that single element.
A legitimate single-owner stage: one public output tensor, so the peer vector sub-block stays idle by design rather than by oversight.
do_not_copy_when: You want a general native-exp accuracy bound. The one-ULP budget here was measured for this stage on A5 over these inputs. It is a statement about this demo, not about `exp`.
You want a complete attention kernel. This is the vector half of a stage pair — read a5_v8_cube_stage for the Cube half, and the MHA or PFA units for a whole kernel.
Your P operand is not in the packed 33-row NZ carrier. The skipped block per fractal column and the three-row tail are properties of that layout, not of the arithmetic.
